_meta.title: Where the sovereign euro goes
_meta.note: An opinionated, sourced trace of who receives European public money for AI and compute infrastructure, and which definition of sovereignty it is measured against. Amounts are as published. Where a figure is not public it is null with disclosed:false and must render as an undisclosed pipe, never as zero. Nothing here is estimated, modelled or derived. Test verdicts are this map's reading of published criteria against public facts, not certifications.

status_vocabulary.committed: budgeted or board-approved, not yet contracted
status_vocabulary.contracted: signed contract or adopted aid decision
status_vocabulary.none: a source positively establishes that no money flows; amount is a confirmed zero, not an undisclosed one
status_vocabulary.declined: the funder was asked and refused, or let the route lapse; amount is a confirmed zero
status_vocabulary.not applicable: no award was possible, so there is nothing to disclose; amount is a confirmed zero

_meta.seeded_by: Cowork research pass 2026-07-25; see RESEARCH-Sovereignty-Definitions-and-Money-Flows_2026-07-25.md for the full sourcing

VARIANTS.name: Operational sovereignty
VARIANTS.measures: Who administers it, from where, and who holds the keys

VARIANTS.name: Technological sovereignty
VARIANTS.measures: Who owns the IP and whether you could fork it
VARIANTS.note: CADA's effective-control test at Annex II 4.1(i)(ii) is defined over SOFTWARE components only.

VARIANTS.name: Jurisdictional sovereignty
VARIANTS.measures: Whose courts and subpoenas reach it

VARIANTS.name: Supply-chain sovereignty
VARIANTS.note: SEAL category SOV-5, weighted 20%, is the only place in any EU instrument where hardware provenance carries weight, and SEAL is procurement documentation, not law. CADA Annex II excludes hardware expressly.

VARIANTS.name: Economic sovereignty
VARIANTS.note: No instrument measures this. IPCEI Communication 2021/C 528/02 point 10(c)(i) makes nationality-of-beneficiary conditions a non-severable violation of Union law. Economic sovereignty is not merely unmeasured, it is legally disfavoured.

TESTS.name: CADA Union assurance level 4
TESTS.legal_status: COM(2026) 502 final, procedure 2026/0138(COD), first-reading start. No EP rapporteur in the official file, no Council position, no trilogue as of 2026-07-25. NOT LAW.
TESTS.deciding_clause: Annex II chapeau: "For the purpose of the criteria under Union assurance levels 1, 2, 3, and 4, 'software' within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2024/2847, Article 3, point (4) falls within the scope of this Annex and Annex III to this Regulation. 'Hardware' within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2024/2847, Article 3, point (5) is outside of the scope."
TESTS.detail: Eleven cumulative criteria at point 4.1, (a) to (k): Union establishment; location of infrastructure, assets and personnel; sensitive customer data, metadata and telemetry remaining exclusively within the Union at any time; personnel who are Union citizens; a European cybersecurity certificate at assurance level high; no use of service-generated data to train third-country AI; not subject to the control of a third country; support performed exclusively within the Union by Union residents; software supply-chain measures including SBOM and effective control over software components; open-source remote-feature controls; separation from any third-country subsidiary. Point 4.1(g) has NO derogation clause, unlike 3.1(g). Commission estimate: roughly 1% of contracts, mainly defence.

TESTS.name: CADA Union assurance level 3
TESTS.deciding_clause: Annex II point 3.1(g) carries a derogation: a third-country-controlled provider "may be audited for Union assurance level 3 where the Commission has adopted an implementing act under Article 19".
TESTS.detail: This is the adequacy-style gate a US hyperscaler subsidiary can pass by Commission decision. Level 4 is closed to third-country control; level 3 is not. Point 4.1(g) states the no-third-country-control criterion with no derogation attached, and the derogation text appears only at level 3, naming Article 19 as the implementing-act route. Commission estimate: under 10% of contracts.

TESTS.name: SEAL-4 (Cloud Sovereignty Framework)
TESTS.legal_status: Procurement documentation used as an award criterion, v1.2.1 October 2025. Applied in the Cloud III tender awarded 2026-04-17. No contract has ever been awarded at SEAL-4.
TESTS.deciding_clause: SEAL-4: "Technology and operations under complete EU control, subject only to EU law, with no critical non-EU dependencies."
TESTS.detail: Eight weighted categories: Strategic 15%, Legal and Jurisdictional 10%, Data and AI 10%, Operational 15%, Supply Chain 20%, Technology 15%, Security 10%, Sustainability 5%. The Supply Chain weighting is the only place hardware provenance is scored anywhere in the EU toolkit. Detailed criteria are withheld under procurement rules (EP question P-004293/2025); the frequently-quoted figure of 48 criteria is Commission-asserted only.

TESTS.name: SEAL-3 (Cloud Sovereignty Framework)
TESTS.legal_status: Highest level actually awarded. April 2026: EUR 180M over six years, four contracts. SEAL-3 to a partnership led by Post Telecom (with OVHcloud and CleverCloud), to STACKIT and to Scaleway; SEAL-2 to Proximus (with S3NS, Clarence, Mistral).

TESTS.name: SecNumCloud 3.2 (France, ANSSI)
TESTS.legal_status: v3.2 dated 8 March 2022, current. A March 2026 decree forces sensitive central-administration data onto it.
TESTS.deciding_clause: Chapter 19.6, "Immunite au droit extracommunautaire". ANSSI requires an EU-registered seat and that non-EU entities "restent minoritaires".
TESTS.detail: The 24% individual and 39% collective non-EU capital caps are verified only in consultation draft 3.2.a, not in the final document. Treat as reported.

TESTS.name: Gaia-X Label Level 3
TESTS.legal_status: Gaia-X's own April 2026 release reports 14 services at Label Level 3 against 600+ catalogued.
TESTS.deciding_clause: P5.1.5 bars non-EU/EEA-headquartered shareholders from holding "control", defined as "decisive influence... de jure or de facto". P5.1.4 requires registered head office, headquarters and main establishment in the EU/EEA. A control test with no percentage threshold.

TESTS.name: BSI C5 (Germany)
TESTS.legal_status: C5:2020 operative until 1 June 2027; C5:2026 published.
TESTS.deciding_clause: Control GC-01 requires the provider to STATE its jurisdiction and the country where the ultimate parent is registered. Nothing requires those to be in the EU.
TESTS.detail: C5 imposes no sovereignty requirement at all. It is disclosure plus security controls, and is routinely misread as a sovereignty credential.

TESTS.name: Chips Act 2.0 "domestic undertaking"
TESTS.legal_status: COM(2026) 504 final, procedure 2026/0139(COD), first-reading start. NOT LAW.
TESTS.deciding_clause: Article 2(31) defines 'domestic undertaking' to include firms "owned and controlled by an undertaking established in a signatory of the WTO Agreement on Government Procurement". Article 2(32) sets ownership at 50% or more.
TESTS.detail: The GPA carve-out admits US, Japanese, Korean and Taiwanese-owned firms as domestic. On procurement preference the teeth are blunt by design: Article 30(1) says authorities "may" require a security-of-supply declaration, 30(2)(c) asks for dual sourcing "where feasible and appropriate", and 30(4)(d) requires any such requirement to be "ancillary and non-decisive in the award of the contract". There is no local-content quota.

CASES.name: ESMC Dresden (TSMC)
CASES.headline: EUR 5bn of German federal money, authorised by the Commission, into a fab 70% owned by a Taiwanese company. This is national money the EU approved, not EU spending: the most commonly mis-stated figure in the file.

Commission AUTHORISATION of national aid. IPCEI Communication 2021/C 528/02 point 10(c)(i) makes nationality-of-beneficiary conditions unlawful, and Chips Act Article 15(1) states that any undertaking may apply, so aid to a non-EU-owned recipient is lawful by design.

Equity: TSMC EUR 3.5bn, each minority partner EUR 500m. Total project investment stated to exceed EUR 10bn. Status as of mid-2026: structural build, tool-in expected 2027, ramp tied to customer demand.

CASES.name: VOLT (Dutch AI Cloud and Rotterdam gigafactory)
CASES.headline: The obvious suspicion does not survive contact with the file: no Dutch and no EU public money reaches VOLT, because the cabinet declined the compute offtake the EU route requires. Confirmed private capital is 'more than ten million euro' against announcements of EUR 5bn to 22.5bn.

chain.note: Reported as "meer dan tien miljoen euro" for phase one: a floor, not a total. An investment bank is separately SEEKING EUR 200m for Rotterdam phase one; that is not raised.

Kamerbrief 2026Z06597 / 2026D14922, from the responsible State Secretary: "Het kabinet constateert dat binnen de huidige begroting geen ruimte bestaat voor het aangaan van de vereiste financiele verplichtingen ten behoeve van de aanbesteding van grootschalige rekencapaciteit bij een AI-gigafabriek." EuroHPC Regulation Art. 12b(4) requires an explicit Member State financing commitment BEFORE the call launches, so the EU route closed for any Dutch bidder. The letter names neither VOLT nor Rotterdam; it is a general policy decision. Dutch public AI-compute money went instead to the Groningen AI factory: EUR 71m cabinet, EUR 200m total.
No award is possible: the AI Gigafactories call had not opened as of 2026-07-25.

chain.note: KvK 98224255, entity registered 2025-09-05. Operating base is 14MW leased at Switch AMS4; first commercial offer is 64 B300 GPUs. Rotterdam gigafactory announced 2026-04-17 at up to 800MW phased, construction earliest 2027. Dutch AI Cloud announced 2026-07-09, go-live stated October 2026, not live.

CASES.name: AI Gigafactories / InvestAI
CASES.headline: EUR 20bn announced, EUR 1bn actually programmed, and the call still had not opened on 25 July 2026. Its own documentation encourages European hardware rather than requiring it, and plans in the same breath for US export restrictions.

chain.entity: EuroHPC grant, capped at 17% of CAPEX
chain.note: Regulation (EU) 2026/150 Art. 12b(5): Union contribution up to 17% of CAPEX, with participating states matching at least that. Art. 12b(3) restricts CONSORTIUM CONTROL to EU entities: it says nothing about chip origin. THE CALL HAS NOT OPENED: the EuroHPC calls page returned "Calls for proposals (0)" when checked on 2026-07-25. Only a preparatory info session was held, on 2026-06-16.

An informal expression of interest closed 2025-06-20. The Commission states 77 proposals across 16 Member States and 60 sites; a figure of 76 also circulates from the EoI. No site selected, no consortium named, no vendor chosen.

test_notes.cada4: Annex II 4.1(g) bars a provider "subject to the control of a third country", and point 4.1(g) carries NO derogation clause.

related.name: Campus AI, Fouju (Seine-et-Marne)
related.note: 1.4GW is a 2030 target, not committed load: a ministry answer of 19 May 2026 records 700MW contracted with the grid operator to date. Shareholdings are reported as MGX 70 percent / Bpifrance 25 percent / Nvidia 4 percent / Mistral 1 percent, reconstructed from partially redacted capital-increase filings and NOT confirmed by the parties. MGX is Abu Dhabi state-created capital. Capital figures conflict across official sources with incompatible scopes: EUR 8.5bn for phase one, EUR 35bn in the public-debate filing, and about EUR 50bn to completion for the whole project including the datacentres and their equipment. An Eiffage substation contract of 2 June 2026 is stated as more than EUR 120m, a floor rather than an exact figure. CASES.name: Nscale and Sines, Portugal
CASES.headline: No Portuguese and no EU public money at the Sines site, on three statements that are all ultimately the facility owner's own and are scoped to the first building. This is US-financed, US-vendored, US-tenanted capacity sited in Europe, with a Norwegian equity anchor and Norwegian state debt.

chain.note: Revolving credit facility. J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, MUFG, RBC, BofA, Credit Agricole CIB, Deutsche Bank, Mizuho, SMBC, TD, KeyBank. Only two are EU banks. Pricing, tenor, collateral and amount drawn are not disclosed, so "committed" is the only defensible status.
Of a USD 790m Narvik project facility: Norway, not Portugal. The minister's defence: "Eksfin gir ikke stotte", finance on the same terms as private banks.

Confirmed three ways, all ultimately the facility owner's own assertion. The environmental compliance report filed with APA, dated AGOSTO 2024 on its cover (October 2024 is only its portal publication date), records shareholders investing approximately EUR 240m "sem utilizacao de quaisquer subsidios, nem fundos publicos, nem qualquer tipo de beneficios fiscais ou financiamento europeu". Start Campus, 4 April 2025: funding provided to privately deliver SIN01 without subsidies, public funds or tax benefits. Portugal Global, the news channel of the state agency AICEP, relaying the company on 7 April 2025: "viabilizaram o SIN01 de forma totalmente privada, sem capital publico (sem recurso a subsidios, fundos publicos, ou qualquer tipo de beneficios fiscais ou financiamento europeu)". The last two are scoped to SIN01 specifically, and Nscale's own release of 5 May 2026 attributes EUR 230m of shared infrastructure and EUR 465m of the second building to Nscale, so the campus as a whole is not shareholder-funded alone. PIN status is a permitting fast-track, not money. Do not conflate with the separate, unawarded EUR 200m approved by the Council of Ministers on 2026-06-26 for compute time in an Iberian EuroHPC gigafactory bid, in which Nscale is not a named member. The landlord's own money chain is a separate case in this ledger.

chain.role_note: Project finance to the concessionaire, committed but not drawn
chain.note: Three facilities signed 14 February 2024: senior line EUR 137m, VAT line EUR 70m, revolving working capital EUR 15m. Mixed private and state capital: CDP is 82.77 percent held by the Italian Ministry of Economy and Finance.
chain.src: Polo Strategico Nazionale S.p.A., Bilancio integrato 2025 (audited by EY)

chain.role_note: Drawn, as distinct from committed
chain.note: EUR 42m drawn on the senior line in 2024 plus EUR 16m in 2025, about 26 percent of the EUR 222m committed. The EUR 7m used on the VAT line in 2024 was repaid during 2025. After year end the company opened talks with lenders on restructuring the debt.
chain.src: Polo Strategico Nazionale S.p.A., Bilancio integrato 2025 (audited by EY)

chain.role_note: Share capital contributed by the four shareholders
chain.note: Share capital EUR 3,000,000; total equity EUR 24,760,913 at 31 December 2025 after a FY2025 loss of EUR 14,572,632 and a FY2024 loss of EUR 11,424,121. Equity is thin relative to a concession with an investment plan of EUR 313.5m.
chain.src: Polo Strategico Nazionale S.p.A., Bilancio integrato 2025 (audited by EY)

chain.entity: PNRR measure M1C1 1.1 public notices to administrations
chain.role_note: The pass-through: EU recovery money reaches PSN as customer revenue, not as a subsidy
chain.note: Published notice endowments include February 2023 EUR 373.8m, March 2024 EUR 224.7m, February 2025 EUR 300m, plus five smaller re-offer waves. These must not be summed: later waves re-offer money to administrations that did not apply earlier, and the February 2025 notice was subsequently increased.

chain.role_note: Public-private partnership concession; the amount is the investment volume in the winning economic and financial plan
chain.note: The concession text records 'l'ammontare degli investimenti previsti nel PEF prodotto dall'operatore economico aggiudicatario, pari ad euro 313.457.176,20'. The performance bond is EUR 130,899,716.82. The tender base d'asta of EUR 4.4bn is a ceiling on the estimated value of 13 years of services, not an appropriation. Article 9 assigns demand, availability, operating and financing risk to the concessionaire, and Article 14(3) expressly permits its obligations to be performed by its own shareholders.

chain.ownership: TIM 45 percent, Leonardo 25 percent, CDP Equity 20 percent, Sogei 10 percent. The Italian State stands behind three of the four: it holds 30.20 percent of Leonardo, 82.77 percent of CDP which wholly owns CDP Equity, and 100 percent of Sogei.
chain.role_note: Concessionaire and operating company
chain.note: FY2025 revenue EUR 454,347,596 against EUR 255,546,505 in FY2024, order backlog about EUR 3,853m, over 600 administrations contracted. This is accrual revenue, not cash received. FY2025 net loss EUR 14,572,632. Control of TIM was in flux at the research date: a full takeover offer from Poste Italiane, itself state-held, ran from 20 July to 11 September 2026.
chain.src: Polo Strategico Nazionale S.p.A., Bilancio integrato 2025 (audited by EY)

chain.entity: TIM, Leonardo, CDP Equity and Sogei, acting as suppliers to the company they own
chain.role_note: The single largest destination of the money
chain.note: The related-party note in the FY2025 accounts records EUR 417,025,964 of PSN's EUR 428,181,206 total service costs, 97.4 percent, incurred with the entities that jointly control it. Named categories: professional services resold to administrations, infrastructure, design and engineering from TIM and Leonardo, lease of equipped space in TIM data centres, connectivity, energy, hardware and software. Trade payables to related parties were EUR 312,298,678 at 31 December 2024. Article 14(3) of the concession authorises this. The split between the four is not published.
chain.src: Polo Strategico Nazionale S.p.A., Bilancio integrato 2025 (audited by EY)

chain.role_note: Supplies the Public Cloud PSN Managed service on Oracle Alloy
chain.note: Oracle's own release states it 'supports an Oracle Alloy region for Polo Strategico Nazionale (PSN) to deliver hyperscale cloud and AI services to the Italian government'. A second amendment to the concession adding Oracle to the Secure Public Cloud offer was being finalised after year end. Amount paid is not published.

chain.role_note: Supplies Hybrid Cloud on PSN's own site via Azure, and Secure Public Cloud on Italian regions
chain.note: PSN's own service description: 'Hybrid Cloud services on the Hub's site are provided by a Cloud Service Provider (Microsoft Azure)'. Amount paid is not published.

chain.role_note: Supplies Public Cloud PSN Managed alongside Oracle, and Secure Public Cloud
chain.note: PSN's own service description names Oracle and Google as the providers of the Public Cloud PSN Managed services. Amount paid is not published.

chain.role_note: Fourth cloud service provider, added to the catalogue in 2024
chain.note: PSN's FY2025 report records 'l'introduzione del quarto CSP AWS' in the 2024 price list. A fifth provider has been identified and proposed to the granting authority. Amount paid is not published.
chain.src: Polo Strategico Nazionale S.p.A., Bilancio integrato 2025 (audited by EY)

not_public: How much PSN pays each of Oracle, Microsoft, Google and Amazon. No figure, no contract value and no share of cost appears in the accounts, on the site, or in the concession documents. This is the largest unmeasured flow in the case.
The split of the EUR 417,025,964 of related-party service costs between TIM, Leonardo, CDP Equity and Sogei individually.
How much of the roughly EUR 700m assigned to administrations has actually been disbursed, spent, or invoiced through to PSN. Only the assignment figure is published.
How much of the EIB's EUR 73m has been disbursed. The EIB publishes signature and tranche sizes, not drawdowns.
Whether the InvestEU EUR 30m sits inside the bank facility, inside the EIB share, or alongside both.
Any breakdown of the EUR 900m PNRR measure between grant and loan financing.
The pricing schedules underlying the concession, including the cloud-provider price list elements.

The damages Italian administrations owe the losing consortium after the Council of State found the pre-emption exercise unlawful in October 2023. The concession's validity was expressly preserved; quantum was still with court-appointed experts in 2026.

test_notes.cada4: Read against the CSP-backed services only. Annex II point 4.1(g) requires that neither the provider nor the subcontractors involved in providing the audited service be subject to third-country control, and it carries no derogation. PSN's Secure Public Cloud and Hybrid Cloud services are provided by Microsoft, Google, AWS and Oracle. The concessionaire itself is Italian-controlled.
test_notes.cada3: Point 3.1(g) does carry a derogation: a third-country-controlled provider may be audited at level 3 where the Commission has adopted an implementing act under Article 19. No such act exists, so this is conditional rather than a pass.
test_notes.chips2-domestic: Chips Act 2.0 governs semiconductor undertakings, not cloud concessions.

CASES.name: Start Campus, Sines (the landlord)
CASES.headline: The company that owns the Sines buildings is private capital from the United States and the United Kingdom held through Luxembourg, and a compliance report filed with the Portuguese environment agency records about EUR 240m of shareholder money with no subsidies, no public funds and no European financing. That statement is scoped to the first building and to August 2024, and the second building is not shareholder-funded alone.

chain.ownership: reported majority shareholder; no percentage is published anywhere
chain.role_note: Private capital, co-founder of the platform in 2020
chain.note: Existence and jurisdiction verified in a primary register: SEC-registered investment adviser, file 801-72222, New York. The 'majority' characterisation appears only in trade press and in the ordering of company boilerplate. No register, filing or company statement gives a percentage, and the Portuguese operating company's LEI record shows no consolidating parent at all.

chain.ownership: reported minority shareholder; no percentage is published
chain.role_note: Private capital, co-founder of the platform in 2020
chain.note: Verified in a primary register: UK limited liability partnership OC339088, incorporated 31 July 2008, London. No amount, percentage or fund name is disclosed on its own portfolio page.

chain.role_note: Tenant, not a shareholder. Money flows from it toward the landlord.
chain.note: This is the boundary of the no-public-money claim. Nscale's release of 5 May 2026 attributes EUR 230m of shared infrastructure and EUR 465m of a second 200MW building to Nscale itself, underpinned by continued shareholder commitment. So the second building is not funded by Start Campus shareholders alone, and the 'privately delivered' framing is scoped to the first. No lease, term, rent or contracted capacity has been published by either party. Nscale's own financing is a separate case in this ledger and is not restated here.

chain.entity: Shareholder equity paid into the project, all shareholders combined
chain.role_note: The only sourced money figure in this case, and it cannot be split between the two shareholders
chain.note: From the environmental compliance report (RECAPE) filed with the Portuguese agency APA. The source says 'cerca de', approximately. It is a proponent self-declaration in a compliance filing, not audited accounts, it is a position as at that date, and it says nothing about the second building. The document is dated AGOSTO 2024 on its cover and history page: October 2024 is only when it was published on the APA portal.
chain.src: RECAPE Data Center Sines 4.0, Volume 2, August 2024, filed with APA

chain.entity: EU public money: subsidies, EU funds, European financing
chain.role_note: A sourced zero, stated three ways
chain.note: Positively established rather than merely absent. The August 2024 RECAPE records shareholder investment 'sem utilizacao de quaisquer subsidios, nem fundos publicos, nem qualquer tipo de beneficios fiscais ou financiamento europeu'. A company release of 4 April 2025 says shareholders 'have provided the funding to privately deliver SIN01 without subsidies, public funds or tax benefits'. Portugal Global, the news channel of the state investment agency, relayed on 7 April 2025 that the shareholders 'viabilizaram o SIN01 de forma totalmente privada, sem capital publico'. All three are ultimately the company's own assertion, and the second and third are scoped to the first building only.
chain.src: RECAPE August 2024; Start Campus 2025-04-04; Portugal Global 2025-04-07

chain.entity: Portuguese state money: subsidies, tax benefits, financial incentives
chain.role_note: A sourced zero at national level
chain.note: Stated by the office of the Secretary of State for Internationalisation at the April 2021 announcement, 'nao foram concedidos quaisquer incentivos fiscais ou financeiros', and repeated in the 2024 filing and the 2025 company statement. The 2021 statement was located only as a quotation in trade-press coverage of the event; no government release or parliamentary answer carrying it was found.

chain.entity: PIN 259, project of potential national interest
chain.role_note: A permitting fast-track. It carries no money.
chain.note: Recognised in March 2021 as PIN number 259, confirmed twice in the August 2024 filing. The regime confers procedural priority and a single point of contact across licensing bodies. It is not a grant, loan, guarantee or tax instrument, and reporting it as a subsidy would be a category error.

chain.entity: Start Campus S.a r.l., Luxembourg holding layer
chain.ownership: holds the capital of the Portuguese operating company
chain.role_note: The interposed vehicle between the funds and the Portuguese asset owner
chain.note: Luxembourg RCS B247750, registered 2020 as Luxembourg Investment Company 399 and renamed in September 2021, share capital EUR 12,002. Its shareholder of record is Start Campus Holdco S.a r.l. Registry particulars were taken from an aggregator rather than read directly from the Luxembourg register, and the filed accounts are paywalled.

chain.entity: Surface right over state-owned ZILS land
chain.role_note: The one point where the Portuguese state is materially involved, and the money runs the other way
chain.note: The August 2024 filing records that the industrial zone is managed by the state agency aicep Global Parques and the land is owned by the state institute IAPMEI. Rent flows from the company to the state. No upfront price, annual rent, term or valuation is published anywhere reachable, so whether the state is being paid market value cannot be established either way. The widely repeated 50-year term and annual rent could not be primary-sourced.
chain.src: RECAPE August 2024 for the land ownership

chain.entity: START Sines TransAtlantic Renewable and Technology Campus, S.A.
chain.ownership: wholly owned through the Luxembourg layer; the split between the two shareholders is not public
chain.role_note: The facility owner and operator, and the subject of this case
chain.note: Portuguese sociedade anonima, LEI 984500C362A57AB6AX45, created 18 March 2020, Lisbon. The EUR 240m recorded on the instrument row is the same money and must not be counted twice here. The LEI record shows no direct or ultimate consolidating parent, filed under the reporting exception for natural persons, so the chain cannot be closed from that register.

chain.role_note: Execution design of the building, substation, data hall cooling and seawater systems
chain.note: Named in the August 2024 filing as author of the execution design with Portuguese partners. No contract value is disclosed for this or any other supplier on the project.

chain.entity: Portuguese design partners (LMSA, Reify, Gapres, Prospectiva)
chain.role_note: Partners on the execution design and the cooling and water systems
chain.note: Named in the August 2024 filing. No contract values disclosed, and their jurisdiction is taken from the filing describing them as Portuguese partners rather than verified in a register.

not_public: The split between Davidson Kempner and Pioneer Point Partners. No percentage appears in any register, filing or company statement, so the 'majority' characterisation is unverified.

The reported Cayman Islands terminus of the holding chain. A December 2023 press investigation describes a cascade across three low-tax jurisdictions starting in the Cayman Islands, citing Portuguese corporate acts it does not publish. The Cayman register is not publicly searchable, no company document names a Cayman vehicle, and an administrator or registered-office provider is not the same as a beneficial owner. Recorded here as reported and unverified rather than drawn as a jurisdiction in the chain.
The historical 76.5 / 23.5 split between an Irish vehicle and a UK vehicle in the December 2020 structure. Press-derived, and superseded in July 2021.
Any contract value for any supplier on the project.
The terms of the surface right over state-owned land: price, rent, term and indexation.
The tenancy terms with Nscale: lease type, term, rent and contracted capacity.

Whether the campus as a whole is free of public money. The three statements are scoped to the first building or to the position in August 2024. Nothing sourced establishes the position for the second building or later phases.

Capacity figures do not reconcile. Four operator figures exist for the first building (15 rising to 29, 26, 31 and 37.5 MW) with no explanation of the differences or whether they are IT load or grid connection. The 1.2 GW campus figure is a marketing capacity number: the consented envelope in the August 2024 filing is 495 MW for the whole campus.

The EUR 8.5bn total campus investment figure appears only as company boilerplate and silently superseded an earlier EUR 3.5bn figure in the 2024 filing, with neither evidenced by a board approval, budget line or contract.

test_notes.cada4: CADA governs cloud computing service providers and their services. Start Campus is a datacentre landlord selling powered shell and build-to-suit space, not a cloud service, so the assurance levels do not reach it.

CONTRADICTIONS.case: EU-owned provider, all-Nvidia estate, TSMC silicon
CONTRADICTIONS.why: CADA Annex II excludes hardware from scope entirely. SEAL weights supply chain at 20% and SEAL-4 requires no critical non-EU dependencies.

CONTRADICTIONS.case: US hyperscaler EU subsidiary, EU regions, EU staff
CONTRADICTIONS.why: Level 3 carries a derogation for third-country-controlled providers by Commission implementing act. Level 4 does not. C5 imposes no sovereignty requirement at all.

CONTRADICTIONS.case: TSMC-owned fab in Dresden receiving EUR 5bn
CONTRADICTIONS.why: Chips Act 2.0 Article 2(31) admits WTO GPA signatories as domestic undertakings. State aid law goes further: IPCEI rules make a nationality condition unlawful.

CONTRADICTIONS.case: EU-controlled provider, 23% US minority equity, dividends flowing out
CONTRADICTIONS.why: CADA 4.1(g) is a CONTROL test, not an equity test, and CADA contains no provision on profits, revenue or economic benefit anywhere in its operative articles. No instrument measures this at all.

CONTRADICTIONS.case: Non-EU parent compelled under 18 U.S.C. 2713 to produce EU-held data
CONTRADICTIONS.why: Data Act Article 32 binds only the EU provider as addressee, and EDPB Guidelines 02/2024 paragraph 8 places the parent-route request outside GDPR Article 48 entirely. No EU instrument resolves the conflict. Demonstrated in practice in June 2026 when a US export-control directive took two frontier models offline worldwide and cut off every EU user for eighteen days.
